Technical input: The comparison from actual reduced hammocks to free simplicial resolution localization, before passing to infinity categories.

title: Free-resolution and hammock presentations of derived simplicial localization
statement:
Use simplicial categories, Dwyer--Kan equivalences and the Bergner model structure of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Let $C$ be a small ordinary category and $W\subseteq C$ a wide subcategory, meaning a subcategory containing every object and its identity. Let $F$ be the free-category comonad: $FC$ has the objects of $C$ and a free generator for each nonidentity arrow of $C$, counit composes words and comultiplication regards each generator as a one-letter word. Its standard simplicial resolution $F_\bullet C$ has degree $n$ equal to $F^{n+1}C$, with faces given by the counit and degeneracies by comultiplication. Let $L(C,W)=F_\bullet C[(F_\bullet W)^{-1}]$, where localization is ordinary arrow inversion in each simplicial degree. The augmentations $F_\bullet W\to W$ and $F_\bullet C\to C$ are identity on objects and weak equivalences on all mapping sets; $F_\bullet W$ and $F_\bullet C$ are cofibrant, and their inclusion is a cofibration.

Define $H(C,W)(x,y)_k$ to be the reduced commutative hammocks with a finite number of horizontal columns and $k+1$ rows, each from $x$ to $y$, all vertical arrows pointing down, identity vertical endpoint arrows, and all other vertical arrows in $W$, horizontal arrows pointing uniformly in each column, leftward arrows in $W$, alternating column directions, and no entirely identity column. The length-zero hammock is allowed exactly when $x=y$. Faces delete a row, degeneracies repeat one, and composition concatenates rows horizontally; in each case reduce by deleting identity columns and composing adjacent like-directed columns. These formulas define a simplicial category $H(C,W)$ and a functor $C\to H(C,W)$ sending an arrow to its one-arrow hammock, or the length-zero hammock when it is an identity. There is a natural span of simplicial functors, identity on objects,
$$H(C,W)\ \longleftarrow\ \operatorname{diag}H(F_\bullet C,F_\bullet W)\ \longrightarrow\ L(C,W),$$
whose arrows induce weak homotopy equivalences on every mapping simplicial set. In the middle term $H$ is applied in each degree and the simplicial diagonal is taken. The span commutes with the maps from $F_\bullet C$ to its two ends, namely augmentation followed by the one-arrow hammock on the left and ordinary inversion on the right. It is natural for functors $(C,W)\to(C',W')$ preserving the distinguished subcategories, including enriched composition. No saturation, two-out-of-three or model-category hypothesis is required on $(C,W)$.

source.place: Definition 2.1 and Proposition 2.2, printed pp.19-20, with Lemmas 2.3-2.4 and Remark 2.5. Standard resolution and cofibrancy: Dwyer--Kan, Simplicial localizations of categories, Sections 2.4-2.6, 4.1, 4.5, 7.6; no Stacks tag states the comparison.

proof.text: First check the diagram formulas. Reduce a grid by scanning its columns left to right: omit an identity column, and if the next column has the direction of the last retained one, replace the two by their composite and repeat if that composite is an identity column. The unit and associativity laws show, by induction on the number of columns, that inserting an identity column or replacing adjacent like-directed columns by their composite leaves this output unchanged. Thus row deletion, repetition, applying a functor and concatenation followed by reduction are independent of intermediate reductions. Before reduction the row operators satisfy the simplicial identities; consequently they do so afterwards. Concatenation is associative and the length-zero grid is its unit. The same invariance gives the interchange of composition with row operators, so these are simplicial categories in the sense of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. A one-arrow grid and its constant repetitions give the asserted functor from $C$; two consecutive rightward columns reduce to their composite in $C$. Identity arrows reduce to the length-zero grid. Applying a subcategory-preserving functor to arrows and reducing is functorial, even if it sends nonidentity arrows to identities.

source.place: Definition 2.1, printed p.19, and Section 3.4; reduction identities expanded by the worker

proof.text: The free-word formulas give the comonad identities: composing a word of one-letter words or composing the outer word recovers the original word, and three levels of brackets can be inserted in either order. Hence the displayed faces and degeneracies define $F_\bullet C$ and $F_\bullet W$. For fixed $x,y$, augment $X_n=F^{n+1}C(x,y)$ to $X_{-1}=C(x,y)$. On underlying sets define $h_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ by regarding an entire nonidentity arrow as one new generator, and send an identity to the empty word; use the same formula for $h_{-1}$. Directly removing or duplicating a level of brackets gives $d_0h_n=1$, $d_{i+1}h_n=h_{n-1}d_i$, $s_{i+1}h_n=h_{n+1}s_i$ and $s_0h_n=h_{n+1}h_n$, with augmentation at degree $-1$. On geometric realization these identities make $([a;(t_0,\ldots,t_n)],u)\mapsto[h_n(a);(u,(1-u)t_0,\ldots,(1-u)t_n)]$ well defined on every augmentation fiber: at $u=0$ it is the original point and at $u=1$ it is the vertex $h_{-1}(\epsilon a)$. Thus every fiber contracts to that vertex and the augmentation is a homotopy equivalence onto the discrete set $C(x,y)$, hence a weak homotopy equivalence by the definition in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For $X^W_n=F^{n+1}W(x,y)$, define $h^W_n$ by the one-generator word of the whole arrow, with identities sent to the empty word. The displayed face and degeneracy identities apply to these words in $W$, since composition and identities restrict from $C$ to $W$. The displayed realization formula therefore contracts each fiber over $w\in W(x,y)$ to $h^W_{-1}(w)$, proving the second augmentation equivalence. Both augmentations fix objects. The empty mapping-set case is empty in every degree.

source.place: Sections 2.4–2.6, printed p.270; the mapping-set contraction is written explicitly, not inferred from an additive chain-complex theorem

proof.text: In degree $n$ put $G_n=F^{n+1}C$ and $V_n=F^{n+1}W$. The generators of $V_n$ are a subset of the generators of $G_n$. The subcategory $D_n$ freely generated by the complementary generators gives $G_n=D_n*_O V_n$, because every word has a unique decomposition into maximal blocks from the two generator sets. Every degeneracy carries an outer generator to an outer generator and preserves the number of outer letters of a word. Apply the unique nondegenerate decomposition of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] to each mapping simplicial set of $G$. A degenerate generator has a generator as its nondegenerate ancestor, since degeneracies preserve outer word length. If that ancestor lies in $V$, so does its degeneracy; conversely if a degeneracy lies in $V$, apply its simplicial face retraction, which preserves $V$, to see that the ancestor lies in $V$. Therefore the generators outside $V$ are exactly degeneracies of nondegenerate generators outside $V$. The same description holds for all generators of $G$ and of $V$.

source.place: Sections 2.4–2.5 and 7.4, printed pp.270 and 277; generator and relative-degeneracy checks expanded, using Stacks Tag 017R (lemma-splitting-simplicial-sets)

proof.text: Here is the lifting proof of the stated Bergner cofibrancy, without changing model structures. Let $p:E\to B$ be a Bergner trivial fibration. By [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] its mapping maps are both Kan fibrations and weak homotopy equivalences, so [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] gives lifts against every $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$. It is surjective on objects: essential surjectivity gives an object over something isomorphic in $\pi_0B$ to any prescribed object, and equivalence lifting supplies an object over that prescribed object. To lift a functor from $G=F_\bullet C$ into $B$, choose lifts of its objects and proceed through nondegenerate generators by dimension. Every face of a dimension-$n$ generator is an arrow in degree $n-1$, hence a word in generators whose nondegenerate ancestors have dimension at most $n-1$, so its image in $E$ is already prescribed. For $n\geq2$, the face-overlap equations $d_i d_j=d_{j-1}d_i$ for $i<j$ hold under the previously constructed maps, yielding a map $\partial\Delta^n\to E(x,y)$; for $n=1$ the two vertices give this map, and for $n=0$ the boundary is empty. It lies over the boundary of the specified simplex in $B(x,y)$, so the boundary lift supplies its whole $n$-simplex. Extend over degeneracies and all composable words. Step 3's unique nondegenerate decomposition ensures consistency; faces agree because the boundary was prescribed, and degeneracies agree by construction. This gives the required simplicial functor. The same proof applies to $F_\bullet W$. For a lifting square from $F_\bullet W\hookrightarrow F_\bullet C$ retain the given object and generator lifts on $F_\bullet W$, and perform this construction only on its complementary nondegenerate generators, which Step 3 shows are closed under taking nondegenerate ancestors. These are lifts against every Bergner trivial fibration. The definitions of cofibrant object and cofibration in the cited Bergner statement prove all three claims.

source.place: Sections 7.4–7.6, printed pp.277–278; explicit free-generator lifting proof in the Bergner structure

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-hammock-pair-homotopy-invariance] to the simplicial pair $(A,U)=(F_\bullet C,F_\bullet W)$, the constant simplicial pair $(B,V)=(C,W)$, and the augmentation. The object set is $O=\operatorname{Ob}C$, all four categories and subcategories are small, the subcategories are wide, the functor fixes objects and preserves them, and both mappingwise weak-equivalence hypotheses were proved in Step 2. Its conclusion is the left arrow $\operatorname{diag}H(F_\bullet C,F_\bullet W)\to H(C,W)$ on every mapping set, since a constant simplicial pair has diagonal hammock category exactly its ordinary hammock category. Its action is to augment every entry and reduce, so it preserves enriched composition by Step 1.

source.place: Lemma 2.4 applied as in the proof of Proposition 2.2, printed p.20

proof.text: For each resolution degree $n$, Step 3 gives the free-factor presentation $G_n=D_n*_O V_n$, with both factors free. Apply [lem-coef-free-factor-hammock-comparison] to obtain $H(G_n,V_n)(x,y)\to G_n[V_n^{-1}](x,y)$ as a weak homotopy equivalence, the target viewed as a discrete simplicial set. Its row formula gives a map of bisimplicial sets: write $v_j$ for the vertical arrow at horizontal position $j$, and $r_j,r_j^\prime$ for the top and bottom row arrows oriented from position $j-1$ to $j$ after inversion of any leftward arrow. Commutativity gives $r_j^\prime=v_j r_j v_{j-1}^{-1}$ in the localization, for a rightward or a leftward column. Thus $r_m^\prime\cdots r_1^\prime=v_m(r_m\cdots r_1)v_0^{-1}=r_m\cdots r_1$, since $v_0=1_x$ and $v_m=1_y$. This proves that all rows have the same localized value, including the empty product. Resolution faces and degeneracies preserve $V_n$ and commute with products and inverses, so they commute with this map; they need not preserve the complementary free factors. By [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] the diagonal is a weak homotopy equivalence. The target diagonal has degree $n$ equal to $G_n[V_n^{-1}](x,y)$, which is precisely $L(C,W)(x,y)_n$. The row-product formula respects concatenation, hence the diagonal map is a simplicial functor and gives the right arrow of the claimed span.

source.place: Lemma 2.3 and Proposition 2.2, printed p.20; diagonal argument also Dwyer–Kan, Simplicial localizations, Section 1.4(vii)

proof.text: The map $F_\bullet C\to\operatorname{diag}H(F_\bullet C,F_\bullet W)$ sends a degree-$n$ arrow to the width-$n$ grid with its one horizontal arrow repeated in all rows. Its left image augments that arrow and repeats it; its right image is its ordinary localized arrow. Thus both triangles with $F_\bullet C$ commute strictly. For a functor of pairs $(C,W)\to(C',W')$, $F$ sends a generator to the generator of its image, or to an identity when that image is an identity. This commutes with the counit and comultiplication. On the middle term the functor applies these resolution functors to grid entries and reduces. Augmentation, rowwise inversion, and reduction commute with that operation, as checked in Steps 1 and 6; both arrows of the span therefore commute strictly with the induced functors and with enriched composition. All arrows in the span fix $O$. The left equivalence used only the two augmentation equivalences, and the right equivalence only degreewise freeness and the diagonal theorem. Neither argument assumes saturation or two-out-of-three for $W$, or a model structure on $(C,W)$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2 and Section 3.4, printed pp.20–21; explicit comparison on generators and on every hammock
